text: On the twenty-ninth of May, 1984 — sixteen years before this accident — McDonnell Douglas issued a service letter to operators.

text: It reported three cases where a jackscrew assembly had come off an aeroplane far earlier than expected, because of excessive play between the screw and the nut.

text: Every nut showed severe wear on the thread surfaces. And the letter records what they found in the lubrication passages of two of them. The grease was dry, and without evidence of recent renewal.

text: The letter concluded that inadequate lubrication was the most probable cause of the wear, and it asked operators to keep to a conscientious lubrication programme.
